THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 24.03.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
Crl.Rev.Pet No.361 of 2026  2026:KER:25825  -3-  JUDGMENT (Dated this the 24th day of March, 2026)

The petitioner is the 3rd accused in S.C No.2362 of 2024 on the file of Fast Track Special Court-I, Neyyattinkara, arising out of Crime No.983 of 2022 of Kovalam Police Station, filed this Crl.Rev.Pet against the order of the special Judge dismissing the application filed by him under Section 250 BNSS.
2.

According to the learned counsel for the revision petitioner, the only allegation levelled against the petitioner is under Section 506(i) IPC and according to him, the allegation levelled against the petitioner does not make out the offence punishable under Section 506(i) IPC.

Therefore, the learned counsel would argue that, the order of the Sessions Judge dismissing Crl.M.P No.126 of 2025 is liable to be set aside and the petitioner is liable to be discharged under Section 250 (c)
BNSS.
3. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. The offences involved in this case are under Sections 376(2)(n), 366, 323, 354, 506(i), 307 and 354B r/w Section 34 of IPC.
It is true that the main offences are alleged only against the 2026:KER:25825 1st accused.

The allegation against the petitioner herein is that the petitioner called the de facto complainant over the telephone, introduced him as the Superintendent of jail and warned her not to call 'Reneesha' (the 2 nd accused) that she belong to a reputed family and in case,
she contacts her, the petitioner will be booked in a honey trap.

5. Section 503, which defines criminal intimidation is as follows:-
"Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threats, commits criminal intimidation."
6. On a perusal of the above definition of the term "criminal intimidation", it can be seen that, a threat to cause injury to reputation also amounts to criminal intimidation.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the allegation is that the petitioner called the de facto complainant over the telephone and intimidated to book her in a honey trap.
The above allegation prima facie amounts to threat to cause injury to reputation and as such, the prayer for discharging the petitioner is devoid of merits.
Therefore, I do not find any irregularity or illegality in the impugned order passed by the learned Special Judge so as to call for interference.
In the result, this Crl.Rev.Pet is dismissed.

It is made clear that the findings arrived in this order are solely for the purpose of determining this Crl.Rev.Pet. and the same shall not be considered as a fining on merit.
Sd/-
